text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Friday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The Baltic Sea Council closed its sixth session in Riga. Its joint communique sees positive progress in the field of the Baltic regional co-operation.

- The Russian deputy foreign minister, Alexander Avdeyev, announced that Russia had decided to recognise Latvia's non-citizens passports as valid documents for entering the country starting September 1.

- The chief of the Latvian army General staff, Colonel Juris Arness, is reported to have resigned. He is likely to be replaced by Gundars Abols, who has just graduated from one of France's military academies.

- The heads of Estonian Tallinna Pank and Latvian Saules Banka say journalists misunderstood an announcement by the president of Tallinna Pank that they are going to buy 100 percent share of the Latvian bank. The merger is not the question of the near future but a strategic goal.
- Ivan Haritonov, alleged leader of Latvian organised crime, recently discharged from prison, is reported to have applied for a French visa. Unofficial sources say he is going to Monaco.

- Russian deputy foreign minister, Alexander Avdeyev, told the Interfax news agency that his country welcomes a possible visit by Latvian Prime Minister Shkele's to Russia but wants it to be filled with real economic and political content.
- Trygg Hansa Latvia group won a tender to become the insurer of the Ave Lat holding, known to be connected to Shkele.
- The newspaper looks at the Estonian economic expansion in to Latvia one year after Hansapank entered the bank market.
- Russian deputy foreign minister Avdeyev called the situation of the Russian-speaking population in Latvia and Estonia a shameful blot which needed to be removed.
- The Latvian development agency reports that it attracted $15 million in investments last year.
